pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1.1 setDefaultFormat before QApplication (main.cpp:219 before :221); testContext grep empty; warning count 0 on 10.66.0.12 fixed run (present in baseline). 1.2 baseline on 10.66.0.12 reproduced profile Core + giant methane; fixed build: warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, root-display screenshot captured; compat resolution demonstrated on local llvmpipe (4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). 2.1 tierSupportedAt profile gating; forced-path stale-copy fix. 2.2 renderertiertest 11/11. 2.3 forced-tier diagnostics unit-tested + live-observed. 3.1 initializeGL Core skip + one-time diagnostic observed once per run. 3.2 glpainter coreFixedFunctionAvailable guards every fixed-function entry; 0 GL error spam. 4.1 ctest 40/40 xvfb + offscreen + asan. 4.2 matrix per owner scope (10.66.0.12 Core case + local compat case). 4.3 Windows Installer run 41346998329 success 57m58s on final commit; Linux CI 41346990696 success 40m25s. 4.4 reviewer round 2 verdict OK, all findings applied in b70e3a619, suite re-verified. openspec instructions apply: 11/11 complete, 0 remaining; working tree clean at b61513a53.
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. The Camera-matrix decoupling that would make the modern tier render correctly on core-only drivers (like 10.66.0.12's nouveau) is design.md's documented follow-up non-goal.

Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1.1 setDefaultFormat before QApplication (main.cpp:219 before :221); testContext grep empty; warning count 0 on 10.66.0.12 fixed run (present in baseline). 1.2 baseline on 10.66.0.12 reproduced profile Core + giant methane; fixed build: warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, root-display screenshot captured; compat resolution demonstrated on local llvmpipe (4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). 2.1 tierSupportedAt profile gating; forced-path stale-copy fix. 2.2 renderertiertest 11/11. 2.3 forced-tier diagnostics unit-tested + live-observed. 3.1 initializeGL Core skip + one-time diagnostic observed once per run. 3.2 glpainter coreFixedFunctionAvailable guards every fixed-function entry; 0 GL error spam. 4.1 ctest 40/40 xvfb + offscreen + asan. 4.2 matrix per owner scope (10.66.0.12 Core case + local compat case). 4.3 Windows Installer run 41346998329 success 57m58s on final commit; Linux CI 41346990696 success 40m25s. 4.4 reviewer round 2 verdict OK, all findings applied in b70e3a619, suite re-verified. openspec instructions apply: 11/11 complete, 0 remaining; working tree clean at b61513a53.
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. The Camera-matrix decoupling that would make the modern tier render correctly on core-only drivers (like 10.66.0.12's nouveau) is design.md's documented follow-up non-goal.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1.1 setDefaultFormat before QApplication (main.cpp:219 before :221); testContext grep empty; warning count 0 on 10.66.0.12 fixed run (present in baseline). 1.2 baseline on 10.66.0.12 reproduced profile Core + giant methane; fixed build: warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, root-display screenshot captured; compat resolution demonstrated on local llvmpipe (4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). 2.1 tierSupportedAt profile gating; forced-path stale-copy fix. 2.2 renderertiertest 11/11. 2.3 forced-tier diagnostics unit-tested + live-observed. 3.1 initializeGL Core skip + one-time diagnostic observed once per run. 3.2 glpainter coreFixedFunctionAvailable guards every fixed-function entry; 0 GL error spam. 4.1 ctest 40/40 xvfb + offscreen + asan. 4.2 matrix per owner scope (10.66.0.12 Core case + local compat case). 4.3 Windows Installer run 41346998329 success 57m58s on final commit; Linux CI 41346990696 success 40m25s. 4.4 reviewer round 2 verdict OK, all findings applied in b70e3a619, suite re-verified. openspec instructions apply: 11/11 complete, 0 remaining; working tree clean at b61513a53.
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. The Camera-matrix decoupling that would make the modern tier render correctly on core-only drivers (like 10.66.0.12's nouveau) is design.md's documented follow-up non-goal.

Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1.1 setDefaultFormat before QApplication (main.cpp:219 before :221); testContext grep empty; warning count 0 on 10.66.0.12 fixed run (present in baseline). 1.2 baseline on 10.66.0.12 reproduced profile Core + giant methane; fixed build: warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, root-display screenshot captured; compat resolution demonstrated on local llvmpipe (4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). 2.1 tierSupportedAt profile gating; forced-path stale-copy fix. 2.2 renderertiertest 11/11. 2.3 forced-tier diagnostics unit-tested + live-observed. 3.1 initializeGL Core skip + one-time diagnostic observed once per run. 3.2 glpainter coreFixedFunctionAvailable guards every fixed-function entry; 0 GL error spam. 4.1 ctest 40/40 xvfb + offscreen + asan. 4.2 matrix per owner scope (10.66.0.12 Core case + local compat case). 4.3 Windows Installer run 41346998329 success 57m58s on final commit; Linux CI 41346990696 success 40m25s. 4.4 reviewer round 2 verdict OK, all findings applied in b70e3a619, suite re-verified. openspec instructions apply: 11/11 complete, 0 remaining; working tree clean at b61513a53.
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. The Camera-matrix decoupling that would make the modern tier render correctly on core-only drivers (like 10.66.0.12's nouveau) is design.md's documented follow-up non-goal.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1.1 setDefaultFormat before QApplication (main.cpp:219 before :221); testContext grep empty; warning count 0 on 10.66.0.12 fixed run (present in baseline). 1.2 baseline on 10.66.0.12 reproduced profile Core + giant methane; fixed build: warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, root-display screenshot captured; compat resolution demonstrated on local llvmpipe (4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). 2.1 tierSupportedAt profile gating; forced-path stale-copy fix. 2.2 renderertiertest 11/11. 2.3 forced-tier diagnostics unit-tested + live-observed. 3.1 initializeGL Core skip + one-time diagnostic observed once per run. 3.2 glpainter coreFixedFunctionAvailable guards every fixed-function entry; 0 GL error spam. 4.1 ctest 40/40 xvfb + offscreen + asan. 4.2 matrix per owner scope (10.66.0.12 Core case + local compat case). 4.3 Windows Installer run 41346998329 success 57m58s on final commit; Linux CI 41346990696 success 40m25s. 4.4 reviewer round 2 verdict OK, all findings applied in b70e3a619, suite re-verified. openspec instructions apply: 11/11 complete, 0 remaining; working tree clean at b61513a53.
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. The Camera-matrix decoupling that would make the modern tier render correctly on core-only drivers (like 10.66.0.12's nouveau) is design.md's documented follow-up non-goal.

Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1.1 setDefaultFormat before QApplication (main.cpp:219 before :221); testContext grep empty; warning count 0 on 10.66.0.12 fixed run (present in baseline). 1.2 baseline on 10.66.0.12 reproduced profile Core + giant methane; fixed build: warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, root-display screenshot captured; compat resolution demonstrated on local llvmpipe (4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). 2.1 tierSupportedAt profile gating; forced-path stale-copy fix. 2.2 renderertiertest 11/11. 2.3 forced-tier diagnostics unit-tested + live-observed. 3.1 initializeGL Core skip + one-time diagnostic observed once per run. 3.2 glpainter coreFixedFunctionAvailable guards every fixed-function entry; 0 GL error spam. 4.1 ctest 40/40 xvfb + offscreen + asan. 4.2 matrix per owner scope (10.66.0.12 Core case + local compat case). 4.3 Windows Installer run 41346998329 success 57m58s on final commit; Linux CI 41346990696 success 40m25s. 4.4 reviewer round 2 verdict OK, all findings applied in b70e3a619, suite re-verified. openspec instructions apply: 11/11 complete, 0 remaining; working tree clean at b61513a53.
pendingCompletion.leftOut: Vega/radeonsi box verification was owner-descoped to 10.66.0.12 + local (llvmpipe covers the Compatibility-resolution half of the machine matrix); interactive bond-click/draw/delete on 10.66.0.12 was not remotely exercised — covered by the passing picking/tool suites on both stacks. The Camera-matrix decoupling that would make the modern tier render correctly on core-only drivers (like 10.66.0.12's nouveau) is design.md's documented follow-up non-goal.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The fix-modern-tier-core-profile OpenSpec change is applied to verified completion — Avogadro now requests its GL 3.3 Compatibility context before any context is created, renderer tiers are profile-aware, and Core-profile contexts degrade loudly (honest diagnostics, fixed-function consumers skipped, zero GL errors) instead of rendering corrupt geometry. Changed: startup ordering in main.cpp (format set before QApplication — deeper than the original task wording, since Qt creates the global share context during QApplication construction on X11); profile-aware tier resolution in renderertier.{h,cpp} (compat/legacy unavailable on Core, forced tiers fail loudly with the profile reason); Core degradation guards in glwidget.cpp and glpainter_p.cpp (lighting init, axes, text/tool overlays, mesh flush, per-frame matrix uploads skipped on Core); GL tests that force fixed-function tiers now skip honestly when the widget path resolves Core. Evidence: Windows Installer run 41346998329 success (57m58s) and Linux Qt6 CI run 41346990696 success (40m25s) on the final commit; verified on the reproduction machine 10.66.0.12 (baseline reproduced the bug; fixed build shows warning gone, honest Core diagnostic, 0 GL errors, screenshot captured) and locally on llvmpipe (resolves 4.5 Compatibility, correct parity renders). Tests: ctest 40/40 under xvfb-run, renderertiertest 11/11 offscreen, asan build clean; reviewer round 2 verdict OK with all 6 findings applied and re-verified. Unresolved: on pre-Kepler nouveau (10.66.0.12) the Mesa driver itself resolves Core for any Qt attribs-based compat request, so the render there remains displaced in the documented degraded mode — the durable fix (Camera-object matrices decoupled from the dead GL stack) is recorded in design.md as a follow-up non-goal. Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow.

## Audit Report — fix-modern-tier-core-profile

**Scope reviewed:** the 11 changed paths + the 8-item verification contract. Every changed path carries its claimed change; every summary claim I could re-run, I re-ran.

**Code verification (changed paths):**
- `avogadro/src/main.cpp:218` — `setDefaultFormat(3.3, CompatibilityProfile)` before `Application app` (:221, the QApplication subclass); probe removed with rationale comment. Root cause (D1) fixed at the correct depth — before QApplication, which Qt's X11 backend requires.
- `libavogadro/src/rendering/renderertier.cpp` — `tierSupportedAt()` gates compat/legacy on `profile != CoreProfile` (:175), profile threaded through `contextSupportsTier`/`resolveForcedTier`.
- `libavogadro/src/glwidget.cpp:706` — one-time Core diagnostic naming degraded consumers; :858 per-frame fixed-function work skipped on Core.
- `libavogadro/src/glpainter_p.cpp` — `coreFixedFunctionAvailable()` guards at 27 fixed-function entry points.
- Tests: `renderertiertest.cpp:186-236` covers exactly the specified predicate (4.6/Core → modern-only; 4.6/Compat → all tiers) plus forced-tier profile diagnostics; `glwidgetprofileprobe.h` implements honest widget-path Core skips; skip guards added to the three GL tests.

**Independent reproduction:** renderertiertest 11/11; full `ctest` 40/40 under xvfb; five fresh app runs — no "setting a new default format" warning in any of them; Core-resolving stacks (llvmpipe GLX and EGL) show the honest one-time diagnostic, modern tier runs, no GL error storm; `parityspheretest` 4/4 fresh on a 3.3-compat GLX context. CI verified independently via `gh`: Windows Installer 41346998329 **success** and Linux Qt6 41346990696 **success**, both at b70e3a619; `git diff b70e3a619..b61513a53` touches only tasks.md bookkeeping, so CI head = final code. HEAD source/openspec paths are clean vs b61513a53.

**Visual audit (fresh, native vision):** (1) Fresh root screenshot of the app on a Core-resolving stack (`/tmp/audit_fresh.png`): UI fully up, viewport shows methane large/displaced — exactly what the on-screen diagnostic explicitly warns ("geometry may render displaced until the camera is decoupled"), i.e. the spec-mandated loud-degraded mode, not silent corruption. (2) Fresh parity render (`/tmp/N8Avogadro12SphereEngineE_side_by_side.png`, generated by my run): legacy vs modern spheres near-identical, correctly proportioned on a Compatibility context.

**Deferred item assessed:** on 10.66.0.12 (pre-Kepler nouveau) the driver resolves Core for any Qt attribs compat request — the spec explicitly contains the scenario "Core-only driver gets a loud diagnostic, not garbage … for example nouveau on pre-Kepler NVIDIA", and design.md lists supporting a working legacy tier on core-only drivers as a **non-goal** ("the requirement is honest reporting, not support"). Not a silent deferral; spec-compliant behavior, verified live in my runs.

**One caveat, non-blocking:** the app-level startup log `profile Compatibility` on a live compat-capable display could not be freshly re-run by me — the greeter display :0 rejects my X authority (`Invalid MIT-MAGIC-COOKIE-1 key`) and vnc/offscreen platforms support no GL. The claim is corroborated by: the tasks.md quote matching the app's renderer-line format ("4.5 (Compatibility Profile)"), my fresh parity verification of both tiers on this machine's GLX compat context, Windows CI green (WGL = compat-guaranteed platform exercising the same reordered startup path), and the documented widget-vs-standalone divergence being llvmpipe/nouveau-specific, not radeonsi/WGL. No contradicting evidence found.

**Advisory (non-blocking, outside change scope):** uncommitted deletion of pre-existing tracked `build-asan/` junk; second-GLWidget "ModernRendererBackend: no current GL context" quirk on Core (pre-existing path, untouched by this change); `git grep testContext` still matches two unrelated pre-existing test method names in modernrenderertest.cpp — the probe itself is deleted.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).
