completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

[OpenSpec 5] 3.1 Rewrite currentModelViewProjection() to read the Camera matrices via composeModelViewProjection
[OpenSpec 6] 3.2 Rewrite currentModelView() to read the Camera modelview

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

[OpenSpec 5] 3.1 Rewrite currentModelViewProjection() to read the Camera matrices via composeModelViewProjection
[OpenSpec 6] 3.2 Rewrite currentModelView() to read the Camera modelview
[OpenSpec 7] 4.1 Narrow the Core diagnostic in initializeGL
[OpenSpec 8] 5.1 Add a headless unit test for the authored perspective/orthographic matrices vs gluPerspective/glOrtho
[OpenSpec 9] 5.2 Run the full affected test suite and confirm no regression

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

## Audit Report — fix-modern-tier-camera-decoupling

I independently verified every contract item against the current tree, re-ran the build and both test suites myself, and mapped all 9 OpenSpec tasks and all 6 spec-delta scenarios to code I read directly.

**Code inspection (changed paths, all confirmed):**
- `libavogadro/src/camera.cpp:42-83` — `perspectiveMatrix`/`orthographicMatrix` are the exact GLU formulas; `applyProjection()` (camera.cpp:285) authors `d->projection` CPU-side with **zero** GL stack calls (`grep` for `gluPerspective|glOrtho|glGetDoublev|glMatrixMode|glLoadIdentity` in camera.cpp matches only comments); deprecated `applyPerspective()` forwards to it (camera.cpp:280-283).
- `libavogadro/src/camera.h:121` — `const Eigen::Projective3d & projection() const` accessor exists.
- `libavogadro/src/glwidget.cpp:851-869` — `applyProjection()` called unconditionally outside the Core guard; non-Core branch uploads the authored matrix via `glMultMatrixd(d->camera->projection().data())`.
- `glwidget.cpp:3445-3451` — pick path: `gluPickMatrix` → `applyProjection()` → `glMultMatrixd` (pick·perspective product preserved).
- `glwidget.cpp:1298-1308` / `1310-1318` — `currentModelViewProjection()` composes from `camera()->projection()/modelview()` via the tested `composeModelViewProjection`; `currentModelView()` reads the Camera modelview with `.transposed()`. Zero `glGetFloatv`.
- `glwidget.cpp:707-717` — Core diagnostic narrowed: lists degraded fixed-function consumers only; says matrices are Camera-authored and decoupled; no displaced-geometry clause.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The modern rendering tier now gets its camera projection/modelview from the Camera's CPU-authored matrices instead of the (dead on Core) GL matrix stack, so molecules render correctly on Core-only drivers.

Changed: Camera::applyProjection() authors d->projection CPU-side (perspective/orthographic formulas, no GL stack calls) with a projection() accessor; paintGL, the GL_SELECT pick path, and paintGL2 upload the authored matrix via glMultMatrixd; currentModelViewProjection()/currentModelView() read the Camera matrices; the Core diagnostic was narrowed; and testCameraProjectionMatchesGLU was added (closed-form 1e-12 + float-rounded live probe at 1e-6) with Core-profile QSKIP guards on the three fixed-function tests.

Evidence: OpenSpec state all_done (9/9 tasks, 0 remaining); GLLA mirror 9/9 complete; fresh-context reviewer OK-with-notes (no code defect); oracle verified the fix on a real GL 4.5 Compatibility context (float-rounded residual exactly 0, confirming the authored matrix matches the stack).

Tests: cmake build (avogadro + modernrenderertest) success; ctest full suite 40/40 pass; modernrenderertest on real GL (xvfb) 20/20 pass with 3 honest Core skips; on the target Core-only GT200 box (10.66.0.12) 20/20 pass + 3 skips and the app resolves Core Profile and selects the modern tier with the authored-matrix diagnostic.

Unresolved: CI runs modernrendererTest offscreen (resolves a Core-only context), so the live compat-context probe QSKIPs there; the closed-form 1e-12 assertions fully cover CI, but the live float-rounded comparison is only exercised on a Compatibility-context developer display.

Next: archive the change via the OpenSpec workflow (subsequent step, out of this goal's scope).

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "fix-orbital-visualization" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "fix-orbital-visualization" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item verification for the completion claim:

1. Task 7.1 (full build): `cmake --build build --parallel 8` exit 0 on the final source (commit 17fa9014c). Verified locally.

2. Task 7.2 (full suite): `/usr/bin/xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure` → 44/44 passed, 0 failed (moleculeBench 105s, screeningTest, cubeevalTest, meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection all green).

3. Task 7.3 (manual matrix): headless modern-tier app smoke test under xvfb (xcb, llvmpipe, GL 4.5 Core) loaded koffein_orca.out and ran the event loop without crash/freeze; per-orbital qDebug removal verified by grep (no per-orbital log in the table-fill loop). Each interactive row maps to an automated regression test: pending/latest-click-wins (orbitalselectionTest), no accumulated connections / no lock leak (surfaceenginehygieneTest), deadlock-free paint (meshlockTest), rendering-tier tests. Full interactive GUI clicking/rotation not exercised (headless).

4. Task 7.4 (perf sanity): `/tmp/perfbench` (High grid 0.05 A, 246x225x136 = 7,527,600 points, koffein 24 atoms) → calculateCubeMO wall_ms=1290, rss_delta_kb=29808 (~29.8 MB, essentially the float result cube 7.53M x 4 bytes). Confirms no per-point-object allocation (old path: ~7.53M x 24-byte GaussianShell + double grid ≈ 240 MB). No before-build comparison available.

5. Task 7.5 (reviewer): reviewer subagent on the full diff returned BLOCKERS: none; 3 actionable findings integrated (gaussianset <algorithm>/<QThread> includes, monotonicity assert on m_atomIndices, cartoonengine stable-before-lock) and 3 accepted trade-offs documented.

6. Task 7.6 (Windows CI): run 41565339293 green — build-installer (installer) passed 45m37s, build-installer (tests) passed 1h2m4s, ctest "100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 44" including autooptreproTest (Passed 25.70s) under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen. This confirms the MSVC waitForFinished fix (the prior run 41561476385 failed at gaussianset.cpp:210 error C2662, now resolved). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (53m19s).

findingGroups.title: Deadlock & engine hygiene
findings: Modern-tier paint no longer self-deadlocks — Mesh::valid() is lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract documented in mesh.h; every call site audited: SurfaceEngine tryLockForRead passes, glwidget flushCapturedMeshes tryLockForRead, cartoonengine stable-before-lock). meshlockTest regression passes.

SurfaceEngine updateOrbitalCombo uses an RAII try-lock guard so the stale-cube early-out can no longer leak a reader; setMolecule disconnects before reconnecting and uses Qt::UniqueConnection, so repeated selections do not multiply per-event work. surfaceenginehygieneTest passes.

findingGroups.title: Responsive orbital UX
findings: Basis load runs off the GUI thread with an epoch guard (stale parse discarded on document switch; parse worker quiesced before m_basis release); per-orbital qDebug removed from the table-fill loop. orbitalselectionTest pins planOrbitalSelection (RenderNow/RenderWhenReady/EnqueueThenRender) and latest-click-wins pending lifecycle.

findingGroups.title: Scalable deterministic evaluation
findings: MO/density evaluation maps over contiguous grid slabs with per-atom shell buckets, max-shell-cutoff atom skip, and thread_local grow-only scratch — no per-point objects; per-point op order unchanged, so results are bitwise identical across slab counts (cubeevalTest 1-vs-4-vs-auto).

OpenQube grid is std::vector<float>; setLimits is geometry-only and grid storage is allocated by the worker (ensureData once before slab spawn), so the GUI thread no longer zero-fills grid buffers. Perf: 7.53M-point High grid MO eval 1290 ms, peak RSS delta ~29.8 MB (≈ the float result cube).

findingGroups.title: Cross-platform
findings: MSVC portability verified: the Windows installer CI caught error C2662 (waitForFinished on const QFuture) which was missed on Linux; fixed by iterating the slab futures as non-const QFuture<void>&. Both installer and tests jobs green; 44/44 tests pass on MSVC including autooptreproTest under offscreen.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

findingGroups.title: Deadlock & engine hygiene
findings: Modern-tier paint no longer self-deadlocks — Mesh::valid() is lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract documented in mesh.h; every call site audited: SurfaceEngine tryLockForRead passes, glwidget flushCapturedMeshes tryLockForRead, cartoonengine stable-before-lock). meshlockTest regression passes.

SurfaceEngine updateOrbitalCombo uses an RAII try-lock guard so the stale-cube early-out can no longer leak a reader; setMolecule disconnects before reconnecting and uses Qt::UniqueConnection, so repeated selections do not multiply per-event work. surfaceenginehygieneTest passes.

findingGroups.title: Responsive orbital UX
findings: Basis load runs off the GUI thread with an epoch guard (stale parse discarded on document switch; parse worker quiesced before m_basis release); per-orbital qDebug removed from the table-fill loop. orbitalselectionTest pins planOrbitalSelection (RenderNow/RenderWhenReady/EnqueueThenRender) and latest-click-wins pending lifecycle.

findingGroups.title: Scalable deterministic evaluation
findings: MO/density evaluation maps over contiguous grid slabs with per-atom shell buckets, max-shell-cutoff atom skip, and thread_local grow-only scratch — no per-point objects; per-point op order unchanged, so results are bitwise identical across slab counts (cubeevalTest 1-vs-4-vs-auto).

OpenQube grid is std::vector<float>; setLimits is geometry-only and grid storage is allocated by the worker (ensureData once before slab spawn), so the GUI thread no longer zero-fills grid buffers. Perf: 7.53M-point High grid MO eval 1290 ms, peak RSS delta ~29.8 MB (≈ the float result cube).

findingGroups.title: Cross-platform
findings: MSVC portability verified: the Windows installer CI caught error C2662 (waitForFinished on const QFuture) which was missed on Linux; fixed by iterating the slab futures as non-const QFuture<void>&. Both installer and tests jobs green; 44/44 tests pass on MSVC including autooptreproTest under offscreen.

findingGroups.title: Deadlock & engine hygiene
findings: Modern-tier paint no longer self-deadlocks — Mesh::valid() is lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract documented in mesh.h; every call site audited: SurfaceEngine tryLockForRead passes, glwidget flushCapturedMeshes tryLockForRead, cartoonengine stable-before-lock). meshlockTest regression passes.

SurfaceEngine updateOrbitalCombo uses an RAII try-lock guard so the stale-cube early-out can no longer leak a reader; setMolecule disconnects before reconnecting and uses Qt::UniqueConnection, so repeated selections do not multiply per-event work. surfaceenginehygieneTest passes.

findingGroups.title: Responsive orbital UX
findings: Basis load runs off the GUI thread with an epoch guard (stale parse discarded on document switch; parse worker quiesced before m_basis release); per-orbital qDebug removed from the table-fill loop. orbitalselectionTest pins planOrbitalSelection (RenderNow/RenderWhenReady/EnqueueThenRender) and latest-click-wins pending lifecycle.

findingGroups.title: Scalable deterministic evaluation
findings: MO/density evaluation maps over contiguous grid slabs with per-atom shell buckets, max-shell-cutoff atom skip, and thread_local grow-only scratch — no per-point objects; per-point op order unchanged, so results are bitwise identical across slab counts (cubeevalTest 1-vs-4-vs-auto).

OpenQube grid is std::vector<float>; setLimits is geometry-only and grid storage is allocated by the worker (ensureData once before slab spawn), so the GUI thread no longer zero-fills grid buffers. Perf: 7.53M-point High grid MO eval 1290 ms, peak RSS delta ~29.8 MB (≈ the float result cube).

findingGroups.title: Cross-platform
findings: MSVC portability verified: the Windows installer CI caught error C2662 (waitForFinished on const QFuture) which was missed on Linux; fixed by iterating the slab futures as non-const QFuture<void>&. Both installer and tests jobs green; 44/44 tests pass on MSVC including autooptreproTest under offscreen.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item verification for the completion claim:

1. Task 7.1 (full build): `cmake --build build --parallel 8` exit 0 on the final source (commit 17fa9014c). Verified locally.

2. Task 7.2 (full suite): `/usr/bin/xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure` → 44/44 passed, 0 failed (moleculeBench 105s, screeningTest, cubeevalTest, meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection all green).

3. Task 7.3 (manual matrix): headless modern-tier app smoke test under xvfb (xcb, llvmpipe, GL 4.5 Core) loaded koffein_orca.out and ran the event loop without crash/freeze; per-orbital qDebug removal verified by grep (no per-orbital log in the table-fill loop). Each interactive row maps to an automated regression test: pending/latest-click-wins (orbitalselectionTest), no accumulated connections / no lock leak (surfaceenginehygieneTest), deadlock-free paint (meshlockTest), rendering-tier tests. Full interactive GUI clicking/rotation not exercised (headless).

4. Task 7.4 (perf sanity): `/tmp/perfbench` (High grid 0.05 A, 246x225x136 = 7,527,600 points, koffein 24 atoms) → calculateCubeMO wall_ms=1290, rss_delta_kb=29808 (~29.8 MB, essentially the float result cube 7.53M x 4 bytes). Confirms no per-point-object allocation (old path: ~7.53M x 24-byte GaussianShell + double grid ≈ 240 MB). No before-build comparison available.

5. Task 7.5 (reviewer): reviewer subagent on the full diff returned BLOCKERS: none; 3 actionable findings integrated (gaussianset <algorithm>/<QThread> includes, monotonicity assert on m_atomIndices, cartoonengine stable-before-lock) and 3 accepted trade-offs documented.

6. Task 7.6 (Windows CI): run 41565339293 green — build-installer (installer) passed 45m37s, build-installer (tests) passed 1h2m4s, ctest "100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 44" including autooptreproTest (Passed 25.70s) under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen. This confirms the MSVC waitForFinished fix (the prior run 41561476385 failed at gaussianset.cpp:210 error C2662, now resolved). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (53m19s).

findingGroups.title: Deadlock & engine hygiene
findings: Modern-tier paint no longer self-deadlocks — Mesh::valid() is lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract documented in mesh.h; every call site audited: SurfaceEngine tryLockForRead passes, glwidget flushCapturedMeshes tryLockForRead, cartoonengine stable-before-lock). meshlockTest regression passes.

SurfaceEngine updateOrbitalCombo uses an RAII try-lock guard so the stale-cube early-out can no longer leak a reader; setMolecule disconnects before reconnecting and uses Qt::UniqueConnection, so repeated selections do not multiply per-event work. surfaceenginehygieneTest passes.

findingGroups.title: Responsive orbital UX
findings: Basis load runs off the GUI thread with an epoch guard (stale parse discarded on document switch; parse worker quiesced before m_basis release); per-orbital qDebug removed from the table-fill loop. orbitalselectionTest pins planOrbitalSelection (RenderNow/RenderWhenReady/EnqueueThenRender) and latest-click-wins pending lifecycle.

findingGroups.title: Scalable deterministic evaluation
findings: MO/density evaluation maps over contiguous grid slabs with per-atom shell buckets, max-shell-cutoff atom skip, and thread_local grow-only scratch — no per-point objects; per-point op order unchanged, so results are bitwise identical across slab counts (cubeevalTest 1-vs-4-vs-auto).

OpenQube grid is std::vector<float>; setLimits is geometry-only and grid storage is allocated by the worker (ensureData once before slab spawn), so the GUI thread no longer zero-fills grid buffers. Perf: 7.53M-point High grid MO eval 1290 ms, peak RSS delta ~29.8 MB (≈ the float result cube).

findingGroups.title: Cross-platform
findings: MSVC portability verified: the Windows installer CI caught error C2662 (waitForFinished on const QFuture) which was missed on Linux; fixed by iterating the slab futures as non-const QFuture<void>&. Both installer and tests jobs green; 44/44 tests pass on MSVC including autooptreproTest under offscreen.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item verification for the completion claim:

1. Task 7.1 (full build): `cmake --build build --parallel 8` exit 0 on the final source (commit 17fa9014c). Verified locally.

2. Task 7.2 (full suite): `/usr/bin/xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure` → 44/44 passed, 0 failed (moleculeBench 105s, screeningTest, cubeevalTest, meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection all green).

3. Task 7.3 (manual matrix): headless modern-tier app smoke test under xvfb (xcb, llvmpipe, GL 4.5 Core) loaded koffein_orca.out and ran the event loop without crash/freeze; per-orbital qDebug removal verified by grep (no per-orbital log in the table-fill loop). Each interactive row maps to an automated regression test: pending/latest-click-wins (orbitalselectionTest), no accumulated connections / no lock leak (surfaceenginehygieneTest), deadlock-free paint (meshlockTest), rendering-tier tests. Full interactive GUI clicking/rotation not exercised (headless).

4. Task 7.4 (perf sanity): `/tmp/perfbench` (High grid 0.05 A, 246x225x136 = 7,527,600 points, koffein 24 atoms) → calculateCubeMO wall_ms=1290, rss_delta_kb=29808 (~29.8 MB, essentially the float result cube 7.53M x 4 bytes). Confirms no per-point-object allocation (old path: ~7.53M x 24-byte GaussianShell + double grid ≈ 240 MB). No before-build comparison available.

5. Task 7.5 (reviewer): reviewer subagent on the full diff returned BLOCKERS: none; 3 actionable findings integrated (gaussianset <algorithm>/<QThread> includes, monotonicity assert on m_atomIndices, cartoonengine stable-before-lock) and 3 accepted trade-offs documented.

6. Task 7.6 (Windows CI): run 41565339293 green — build-installer (installer) passed 45m37s, build-installer (tests) passed 1h2m4s, ctest "100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 44" including autooptreproTest (Passed 25.70s) under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen. This confirms the MSVC waitForFinished fix (the prior run 41561476385 failed at gaussianset.cpp:210 error C2662, now resolved). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (53m19s).

findingGroups.title: Deadlock & engine hygiene
findings: Modern-tier paint no longer self-deadlocks — Mesh::valid() is lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract documented in mesh.h; every call site audited: SurfaceEngine tryLockForRead passes, glwidget flushCapturedMeshes tryLockForRead, cartoonengine stable-before-lock). meshlockTest regression passes.

SurfaceEngine updateOrbitalCombo uses an RAII try-lock guard so the stale-cube early-out can no longer leak a reader; setMolecule disconnects before reconnecting and uses Qt::UniqueConnection, so repeated selections do not multiply per-event work. surfaceenginehygieneTest passes.

findingGroups.title: Responsive orbital UX
findings: Basis load runs off the GUI thread with an epoch guard (stale parse discarded on document switch; parse worker quiesced before m_basis release); per-orbital qDebug removed from the table-fill loop. orbitalselectionTest pins planOrbitalSelection (RenderNow/RenderWhenReady/EnqueueThenRender) and latest-click-wins pending lifecycle.

findingGroups.title: Scalable deterministic evaluation
findings: MO/density evaluation maps over contiguous grid slabs with per-atom shell buckets, max-shell-cutoff atom skip, and thread_local grow-only scratch — no per-point objects; per-point op order unchanged, so results are bitwise identical across slab counts (cubeevalTest 1-vs-4-vs-auto).

OpenQube grid is std::vector<float>; setLimits is geometry-only and grid storage is allocated by the worker (ensureData once before slab spawn), so the GUI thread no longer zero-fills grid buffers. Perf: 7.53M-point High grid MO eval 1290 ms, peak RSS delta ~29.8 MB (≈ the float result cube).

findingGroups.title: Cross-platform
findings: MSVC portability verified: the Windows installer CI caught error C2662 (waitForFinished on const QFuture) which was missed on Linux; fixed by iterating the slab futures as non-const QFuture<void>&. Both installer and tests jobs green; 44/44 tests pass on MSVC including autooptreproTest under offscreen.

Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

findingGroups.title: Deadlock & engine hygiene
findings: Modern-tier paint no longer self-deadlocks — Mesh::valid() is lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract documented in mesh.h; every call site audited: SurfaceEngine tryLockForRead passes, glwidget flushCapturedMeshes tryLockForRead, cartoonengine stable-before-lock). meshlockTest regression passes.

SurfaceEngine updateOrbitalCombo uses an RAII try-lock guard so the stale-cube early-out can no longer leak a reader; setMolecule disconnects before reconnecting and uses Qt::UniqueConnection, so repeated selections do not multiply per-event work. surfaceenginehygieneTest passes.

findingGroups.title: Responsive orbital UX
findings: Basis load runs off the GUI thread with an epoch guard (stale parse discarded on document switch; parse worker quiesced before m_basis release); per-orbital qDebug removed from the table-fill loop. orbitalselectionTest pins planOrbitalSelection (RenderNow/RenderWhenReady/EnqueueThenRender) and latest-click-wins pending lifecycle.

findingGroups.title: Scalable deterministic evaluation
findings: MO/density evaluation maps over contiguous grid slabs with per-atom shell buckets, max-shell-cutoff atom skip, and thread_local grow-only scratch — no per-point objects; per-point op order unchanged, so results are bitwise identical across slab counts (cubeevalTest 1-vs-4-vs-auto).

OpenQube grid is std::vector<float>; setLimits is geometry-only and grid storage is allocated by the worker (ensureData once before slab spawn), so the GUI thread no longer zero-fills grid buffers. Perf: 7.53M-point High grid MO eval 1290 ms, peak RSS delta ~29.8 MB (≈ the float result cube).

findingGroups.title: Cross-platform
findings: MSVC portability verified: the Windows installer CI caught error C2662 (waitForFinished on const QFuture) which was missed on Linux; fixed by iterating the slab futures as non-const QFuture<void>&. Both installer and tests jobs green; 44/44 tests pass on MSVC including autooptreproTest under offscreen.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.

findingGroups.title: Deadlock & engine hygiene
findings: Modern-tier paint no longer self-deadlocks — Mesh::valid() is lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract documented in mesh.h; every call site audited: SurfaceEngine tryLockForRead passes, glwidget flushCapturedMeshes tryLockForRead, cartoonengine stable-before-lock). meshlockTest regression passes.

SurfaceEngine updateOrbitalCombo uses an RAII try-lock guard so the stale-cube early-out can no longer leak a reader; setMolecule disconnects before reconnecting and uses Qt::UniqueConnection, so repeated selections do not multiply per-event work. surfaceenginehygieneTest passes.

findingGroups.title: Responsive orbital UX
findings: Basis load runs off the GUI thread with an epoch guard (stale parse discarded on document switch; parse worker quiesced before m_basis release); per-orbital qDebug removed from the table-fill loop. orbitalselectionTest pins planOrbitalSelection (RenderNow/RenderWhenReady/EnqueueThenRender) and latest-click-wins pending lifecycle.

findingGroups.title: Scalable deterministic evaluation
findings: MO/density evaluation maps over contiguous grid slabs with per-atom shell buckets, max-shell-cutoff atom skip, and thread_local grow-only scratch — no per-point objects; per-point op order unchanged, so results are bitwise identical across slab counts (cubeevalTest 1-vs-4-vs-auto).

OpenQube grid is std::vector<float>; setLimits is geometry-only and grid storage is allocated by the worker (ensureData once before slab spawn), so the GUI thread no longer zero-fills grid buffers. Perf: 7.53M-point High grid MO eval 1290 ms, peak RSS delta ~29.8 MB (≈ the float result cube).

findingGroups.title: Cross-platform
findings: MSVC portability verified: the Windows installer CI caught error C2662 (waitForFinished on const QFuture) which was missed on Linux; fixed by iterating the slab futures as non-const QFuture<void>&. Both installer and tests jobs green; 44/44 tests pass on MSVC including autooptreproTest under offscreen.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item verification for the completion claim:

1. Task 7.1 (full build): `cmake --build build --parallel 8` exit 0 on the final source (commit 17fa9014c). Verified locally.

2. Task 7.2 (full suite): `/usr/bin/xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure` → 44/44 passed, 0 failed (moleculeBench 105s, screeningTest, cubeevalTest, meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection all green).

3. Task 7.3 (manual matrix): headless modern-tier app smoke test under xvfb (xcb, llvmpipe, GL 4.5 Core) loaded koffein_orca.out and ran the event loop without crash/freeze; per-orbital qDebug removal verified by grep (no per-orbital log in the table-fill loop). Each interactive row maps to an automated regression test: pending/latest-click-wins (orbitalselectionTest), no accumulated connections / no lock leak (surfaceenginehygieneTest), deadlock-free paint (meshlockTest), rendering-tier tests. Full interactive GUI clicking/rotation not exercised (headless).

4. Task 7.4 (perf sanity): `/tmp/perfbench` (High grid 0.05 A, 246x225x136 = 7,527,600 points, koffein 24 atoms) → calculateCubeMO wall_ms=1290, rss_delta_kb=29808 (~29.8 MB, essentially the float result cube 7.53M x 4 bytes). Confirms no per-point-object allocation (old path: ~7.53M x 24-byte GaussianShell + double grid ≈ 240 MB). No before-build comparison available.

5. Task 7.5 (reviewer): reviewer subagent on the full diff returned BLOCKERS: none; 3 actionable findings integrated (gaussianset <algorithm>/<QThread> includes, monotonicity assert on m_atomIndices, cartoonengine stable-before-lock) and 3 accepted trade-offs documented.

6. Task 7.6 (Windows CI): run 41565339293 green — build-installer (installer) passed 45m37s, build-installer (tests) passed 1h2m4s, ctest "100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 44" including autooptreproTest (Passed 25.70s) under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen. This confirms the MSVC waitForFinished fix (the prior run 41561476385 failed at gaussianset.cpp:210 error C2662, now resolved). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (53m19s).

findingGroups.title: Deadlock & engine hygiene
findings: Modern-tier paint no longer self-deadlocks — Mesh::valid() is lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract documented in mesh.h; every call site audited: SurfaceEngine tryLockForRead passes, glwidget flushCapturedMeshes tryLockForRead, cartoonengine stable-before-lock). meshlockTest regression passes.

SurfaceEngine updateOrbitalCombo uses an RAII try-lock guard so the stale-cube early-out can no longer leak a reader; setMolecule disconnects before reconnecting and uses Qt::UniqueConnection, so repeated selections do not multiply per-event work. surfaceenginehygieneTest passes.

findingGroups.title: Responsive orbital UX
findings: Basis load runs off the GUI thread with an epoch guard (stale parse discarded on document switch; parse worker quiesced before m_basis release); per-orbital qDebug removed from the table-fill loop. orbitalselectionTest pins planOrbitalSelection (RenderNow/RenderWhenReady/EnqueueThenRender) and latest-click-wins pending lifecycle.

findingGroups.title: Scalable deterministic evaluation
findings: MO/density evaluation maps over contiguous grid slabs with per-atom shell buckets, max-shell-cutoff atom skip, and thread_local grow-only scratch — no per-point objects; per-point op order unchanged, so results are bitwise identical across slab counts (cubeevalTest 1-vs-4-vs-auto).

OpenQube grid is std::vector<float>; setLimits is geometry-only and grid storage is allocated by the worker (ensureData once before slab spawn), so the GUI thread no longer zero-fills grid buffers. Perf: 7.53M-point High grid MO eval 1290 ms, peak RSS delta ~29.8 MB (≈ the float result cube).

findingGroups.title: Cross-platform
findings: MSVC portability verified: the Windows installer CI caught error C2662 (waitForFinished on const QFuture) which was missed on Linux; fixed by iterating the slab futures as non-const QFuture<void>&. Both installer and tests jobs green; 44/44 tests pass on MSVC including autooptreproTest under offscreen.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Applied the OpenSpec change "fix-orbital-visualization" to verified completion — the modern-tier orbital paint freeze, the surface-engine lock leak and duplicate connections, the GUI-thread basis-load stall, the silent not-ready orbital clicks, and the O(grid)×object cube-evaluation memory wall are all fixed.

Changed: Mesh::valid() is now lock-free (caller-held-read-lock contract, audited at every call site); SurfaceEngine releases every mesh lock on every exit path and setMolecule is idempotent; OrbitalExtension loads the basis off the GUI thread with an epoch guard and always responds to orbital selection (latest click wins); MO/density cube evaluation uses slab workers with per-atom shell buckets and thread-local scratch (no per-point objects); the OpenQube grid is single precision and grid storage is allocated by the calculating worker, not the GUI thread.

Evidence: Commits 8cb5b8f24 (implementation), adfaa39db (reviewer findings), 17fa9014c (MSVC waitForFinished fix), 0b1b2715d (verification tasks) on master. Windows Installer CI run 41565339293 green (both build-installer jobs; 100% tests passed, 0 failed, out of 44 on MSVC, incl. autooptreproTest under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen). Linux Qt6 CI run 41564496106 green (python=ON build validates the setData Python binding). Reviewer (7.5) reported BLOCKERS: none.

Tests: Local full suite 44/44 pass under xvfb (cmake --build build --parallel 8 && xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build). Targeted: meshlock, surfaceenginehygiene, orbitalselection, cubeeval (bitwise 1-vs-4-vs-auto determinism), screening (float-aware), precalcpolicy, surfaceextensionmothrottle. Windows MSVC 44/44.

Unresolved: 7.3 manual matrix was verified via the automated regression tests plus a headless modern-tier app smoke test (ORCA file loads, no crash/freeze, no per-orbital log flood); the full interactive GUI matrix (live clicking/rotating) was not exercised in this headless environment. 7.4 perf sanity measured the after-build only (no pre-change comparison); the structural no-per-point-allocation claim is confirmed by RSS delta ≈ result cube size. Accepted reviewer trade-offs (pre-existing, documented): m_minValue/m_maxValue unsynchronized slab writes, lock-free valid() contract for external painters, and the nested-QtConcurrent pool-wait shape.

Next: none.
